cohort: The study included 367 infant patients (neonatal and pediatric) from whom 439 carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) isolates were recovered.
finding: Cesarean section, acidosis, respiration failure, gastric lavage, and enema were identified as independent risk factors for rectal colonization with CPE in 0-3 day old neonates, while cesarean section, cephalosporins, gastric lavage, and residence in rural areas were risk factors for 4-28 day old neonates.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as an independent risk factor for rectal colonization with carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) in both 0-3 day old and 4-28 day old neonatal patients.
cross-section timing: Data were collected during two distinct stool screening periods across three age groups: 0-3 days old, 4-28 days old, and 29 days old to 1 year old.
